OVERCOMING
BARRIERS
WHAT YOU NEED TO DO
Overcoming Barriers
Expect barriers and see them as an opportunity to learn and develop.
Be ready for the barriers. Identify new solutions (more than just one).
Don't give up when barriers arise!
Mistakes made in your business are great learning opportunities – value them!
Use your resources to overcome barriers. Think about what you have, what you know
and who you know.
Keep notes on any actions you take to overcome barriers. They will help you
prepare for future barriers.
Don’t allow your frustration with a barrier to distract you, concentrate all your energies
on working out how to overcome it.
Don't overreact, take a step back and check if the barrier is as big as it seems.
Case study: Luka’s Restaurant
Luka’s Restaurant is a typical place where you can buy meat,
fish and vegetable dishes. The food is greasy but edible. The
inside is a bit run down and the prices are average.
Luka, the owner of the restaurant, is upset. He sponsored new
shirts for the local school football team. However, he often sees
families eating in his competitors' restaurants with children
wearing his shirts!. He is frustrated by these ungrateful families.
Luka has also increased his marketing efforts. Once a week he
hires a student to distribute flyers with his weekly offers
throughout the city. This costs 1,000 Ksh each week. But, so far
he hasn’t seen any increase in business. When Luka goes
home in the evening, he often sees his leaflets discarded on the
roadside and feels even more depressed.

Although he knows the wages he pays are quite low, Luka is also
angry with his employees because they aren’t loyal and often quit. It
also takes him a long time to find and train new employees.
During bad months, when there are too few customers, Luka has to
dip into his own pocket to buy new ingredients.
Last week, Luka’s sister Sadiki, who lives abroad and sends money,
told him she’s not willing to support Luka's restaurant any more.
Although he thinks he knows what to do, once again, Luka seems to
be stuck.
(adapted from J. Matson, 1996)

EXERCISE:
Identifying Barriers
1. Describe the problem
Note the problem
2. Specify the problem
Answer all the questions: What, when / how often? Where? Who?
Why? This makes the problem clearer and finding solutions easier.
3. Think of as many ways as possible to solve the problem:
o Use your creativity to find different sources of information that can
help solve the problem.
o Involve your employees, friends, family, suppliers....
4. Specify (and record) the activities needed to solve the problem.
